findings.source_quote: καὶ περὶ τῶν λίθων τῶν ἀπεληλυθότων εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν καὶ πάλιν ἠρμένων καὶ εἰς τόπον ἴδιον ἀποτεθειμένων
findings.english_quote: And what about the stones that went into the building, were removed again and put back in their own place?
findings.issue: “Put back” introduces a return to a previous location. The selected Greek describes stones removed again and deposited in a place of their own; it does not identify that place as their former location. The source's πάλιν belongs to their removal, already represented by “removed again.”
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “And what about the stones that went into the building, were removed again and set aside in a place of their own?”

findings.source_quote: καὶ περὶ τῆς πέτρας καὶ πύλης καὶ τῶν ὀρέων καὶ τῶν παρθένων
findings.english_quote: Retain the gate/rock relationship, shared load-bearing, condition on understanding and the tower lord’s inspection.
findings.issue: The theological metadata claims to retain a gate/rock relationship and shared load-bearing in this unit. This section names the rock and gate as subjects of Hermas's inquiry but does not describe their relationship or shared load-bearing. The metadata therefore misstates what the selected passage and its translation preserve.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the metadata to describe this unit's actual contents: Hermas's questions about the listed objects, the condition on understanding, and the tower lord's inspection. If the relationship and load-bearing refer to earlier units, identify them explicitly as cross-unit context rather than translated assertions here.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα ἐάν τινες λίθοι σαπροὶ εὑρεθῶσιν, ἀλλάξῃ αὐτούς
findings.english_quote: He must replace any unsound stones he finds.
findings.issue: “Must replace” adds an explicit obligation or necessity not expressed by this purpose clause. The Greek explains the purpose of the inspection: so that, if unsound stones are found, he may replace them. The necessity attached to completion of the tower must not be transferred into a new obligation imposed on its lord.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “He comes to test it so that he can replace any stones found unsound.” Preserve the preceding condition that the tower cannot yet be completed unless its lord comes and tests it.

findings.source_quote: καὶ περὶ τῶν λίθων τῶν ἀπεληλυθότων εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν καὶ πάλιν ἠρμένων καὶ εἰς τόπον ἴδιον ἀποτεθειμένων
findings.english_quote: What about the stones that were used, then removed and put back where they came from?
findings.issue: “Where they came from” explicitly identifies the destination as the stones' original location, which the selected Greek does not do. It says they were deposited in a place of their own after removal. The simplification strengthens the standard edition's unsupported “put back” into a definite claim about their origin.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “What about the stones that went into the building, were removed again and set aside in their own separate place?”

findings.source_quote: καὶ περὶ τῆς πέτρας καὶ πύλης καὶ τῶν ὀρέων καὶ τῶν παρθένων
findings.english_quote: Retain the gate/rock relationship, shared load-bearing, condition on understanding and the tower lord’s inspection.
findings.issue: The theological metadata attributes a gate/rock relationship and shared load-bearing to this unit, although the selected passage only lists the rock and gate among the subjects of inquiry. These are not assertions preserved by this section's simplified translation.
findings.suggested_revision: Limit this metadata to the questions, conditional promise of understanding, and inspection narrated here. Label any discussion of earlier load-bearing or rock/gate relationships as cross-unit context.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τῶν λίθων τῶν ἐκ τοῦ βυθοῦ ἀναβεβηκότων καὶ μὴ λελατομημένων, ἀλλ᾿ οὕτως ἀπελθόντων εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν.
findings.english_quote: Retain rock/gate distinctions, shared carrying, stone counts, the explicitly conjectural negative and the distinction between a pause and completion; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata incorrectly describes this unit as retaining “shared carrying” and an “explicitly conjectural negative.” Shared carrying is not narrated here, and this section's negative is explicit in the selected working Greek. The supplied evidence locates the conjectural negative at S.9.iii.3, not S.9.v.3; footnote c correctly distinguishes those cases.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “shared carrying” from the description of this unit. State that the translation preserves the explicit negative here and that the note explains its contextual relevance to the separately disclosed conjecture at S.9.iii.3.

summary: Both editions cover all seven paragraphs but require revision. Both introduce an unsupported return location for the removed stones and contain out-of-scope metadata. The simplified edition additionally turns the inspection's purpose into a mandatory replacement obligation and mislabels this section's explicit negative as conjectural. The disclosed bracketed readings, numerical alternatives, and long supplement are compatible with the supplied bounded project reports; this review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. All proposed replacements require fresh review.
